To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the canine gene, spanning approximately 8.5 kilobase sequence, consists of five exons and encodes a 116 amino acid protein, and that the canine ortholog of TCTE1 is ubiquitously expressed and down-regulated in the retinas in two forms of inherited retinopathies.

(1) we cloned, sequenced, and characterized the canine TCTE11 gene, (2) we compared the canine gene to the human gene, and (3) we found that the canine gene is ubiquitously expressed, and secondarily expressed in the retina.
the canine TCTEIL gene has five exons and is expressed in all the examined tissues, and is secondarily down-regulated in the retina of two non-allelie forms of inherited retinopathies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of a novel gene, TCTE1, and its expression in the canine model for inherited retinal diseases.
the identification and characterization of the canine ortholog of the human t-complex-associated TCTE1 gene.
the cloning and characterization of a canine TCTEIL gene, and the comparative analysis of the canine gene to its ortholog in humans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TCTE1 gene family is a conserved gene family, which has a common ancestral origin and has been maintained in the mammalian genome.
the canine TCTE11L gene, which encodes an RNA-binding protein, is highly conserved among the species and is a candidate for inherited retinal diseases.
the canine TCTEIL gene is highly conserved in the coding region and the gene flanking sequences, but not in the 3' UTR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the canine gene is orthologous to the murine gene, and the human ortholog is paralogous to the murines.
the canine TCTE11L gene is highly conserved, and the expression is not restricted to the testis, but is ubiquitous, and is down-regulated in the retina of the affected animals.
the canine TCTE11 gene has been characterized and its expression in the tissues examined is consistent with that of the murine ortholog.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dog is a suitable model for studying human retinal diseases.
the canine ortholog of the human TCTE1 is a highly conserved gene, with a high level of expression in most tissues.
TCTE1 is a conserved gene in mammals.
